## Peonies  
China, Qing dynasty (1644- 1911), 18th century  Kei (silk tapestry) with metallic threads, hanging scroll, 98.8 x 54 cm  Collector's seal: Lantang shanwu  Gift of Dr. Ivan Kwok Pun  HKUT.2008.1672  
Recognised as the 'King of Flowers' and a symbol of wealth and honour, blossoming peonies express the wish 'baekje jang' (may you be prosperous), and have traditionally been featured on objects owned by scholars and nobles. The brightly coloured peonies and leaves were woven in various shades of red, pink, orange and green with threads using the changshuang(彩) and short propping' techniques. In dazzling golden ground was created with the kejin (silk tapestry woven with gold') technique, in which twisted gold threads are made by wrapping a yellow silk thread with thin sheets of gold leaf in a spiral twist. This technique provides the tapestry a particularly luxurious and elegant appearance.  
"The seal lantang shanw refers to the Lantang shanwu (Blue Pool Studio) owned by Li Wuhuo (b.1929), a connoisseur and art collector in Hong Kong. Having graduated from the Northwest College of Fine Arts in 1950, Li taught designs, painting and art history at the Grantham College of Education until his retirement in 1984.
